cues.text: Some shirts are great for wash and press. Some are safer dry cleaned, even if the label says you can wash them.
Green means yes. White and light cotton shirts are perfect for wash and press.
Cotton and polyester blends, and classic shirt fabrics like oxford, poplin, and broadcloth, are also great.
Everyday business shirts are the most common wash and press shirts.
Yellow means be careful. Very dark or bright colors can fade, and the hot press can leave shiny marks.
Linen can shrink and get crushed. Stretch shirts can lose their stretch in the heat.
Mother-of-pearl and fancy buttons can crack in the shirt press. Point them out on the ticket.
Red means dry clean. Silk shirts and blouses should always be dry cleaned.
Rayon and viscose shrink and get weak in water, so dry clean them.
Shirts with embroidery, beads, sequins, or lace should be dry cleaned and pressed by hand.
Very thin, vintage, or designer shirts are safer dry cleaned too.
Fitted blouses and shirts with ruffles do not fit the shirt machine. Dry clean them.
When you are not sure, choose dry clean, and ask a manager.
